label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with d/w/0/f/z/c/u
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step (96% of activation mass; never during the original phase, and a small tail at the first one or two copy steps). Within <DEL> steps, the rate climbs steeply with L (rate 0.2% at L=3 up to 7% of steps at t=9; L>=8 holds about 85% of the mass). It is further gated by which tokens open the sequence, i.e. the first outputs about to be produced: the first token (and to a lesser degree the second) in {d, w, 0, f, z, c, u} gives the largest lift (out_tok d/w/0 about 7x). The top activations are 9-token sequences beginning with d/w/0 followed by 0/c/z. This looks like a graded combination of length and first-token identity, not a sharp rule. A boolean predicate gets dev F1 about 0.6 and mass recall about 0.76; many weak activations at <DEL> fall outside it. It does not fire on original-phase inputs or on later copy steps.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: d, w, 0, f, c, z; least: v, y, g, j) and the next token to output (most: 0, f, z, c, d, w; least: j, y, v, g); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, to_go=7.
